summary: Slovakia is an EU and Schengen member: EU/EEA citizens enter freely with an ID card, some 60 visa-waiver nationalities — including the US, UK, Japan and most of the Americas — get 90 days in any 180 across the whole Schengen Area, and other travelers need a Schengen visa.

defaultStayWindow.text: 90 days in any rolling 180-day period, counted across the whole Schengen Area rather than per country. The day you arrive counts as the first day and the day you leave counts as the last. Leaving and coming back does not reset the allowance: on any given day, days already spent anywhere in the area during the preceding 180 still count against the 90.

fee.notes: Standard Schengen fee for adults; children aged 6–12 pay €45.

fee.notes: Indicative fee for stays over 90 days (work, study, family) under Slovak national rules. Confirm with the Slovak embassy.

passportValidity.text: Your passport must be valid for at least 3 months beyond your planned departure from the Schengen Area and have been issued within the previous 10 years. EU/EEA and Swiss citizens can enter with a passport or national ID card.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs of the Slovak Republic

travelInsurance.text: Schengen visa applicants must show travel medical insurance with at least €30,000 of cover valid across the Schengen Area. Visa-waiver visitors are not checked, but cover is strongly recommended; EU citizens can use the EHIC.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs of the Slovak Republic

onwardTicket.text: Not routinely checked, but border officers may ask visa-waiver visitors about return plans, accommodation and means of support.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs of the Slovak Republic

proofOfFunds.text: Slovak rules cite an indicative €56 per person per day of stay. It is rarely checked systematically, but officers may ask non-EU visitors to demonstrate means.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs of the Slovak Republic

currencyLimits.text: Cash of €10,000 or more must be declared when entering or leaving the EU. There are no controls at internal Schengen borders.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs of the Slovak Republic

notes: Standard EU allowances apply to alcohol and tobacco brought from outside the EU.

payments.text: Cards and contactless are accepted almost everywhere, including small-town shops and supermarkets; keep a few euro coins for mountain huts, small kiosks and public toilets.

safety.text: Slovakia is a safe, low-crime country. Petty theft can occur around Bratislava's main station and busy tourist spots; in the High Tatras, respect weather warnings and stay on marked trails.

source.name: U.S. Department of State — Slovakia Travel Advisory

bestTimeToVisit.text: May to September is best for Bratislava, the castles and High Tatras hiking; December to March is ski season in the Tatras and Low Tatras.

roadVignette.appliesTo: Two-track vehicles up to 3.5 t and every M1 car whatever its weight; if car plus trailer exceeds 3.5 t the trailer needs a second vignette.
roadVignette.text: Slovakia charges for marked sections of its motorways and expressways with an electronic vignette tied to the number plate. Eznamka.sk is the only official sales channel online, alongside the operator's points of sale at fuel stations and border crossings. A 10-day or 30-day vignette bought in December stays valid into January.

source.name: Národná diaľničná spoločnosť — Types and prices of vignettes

idp.text: Slovakia is a party to both the 1949 Geneva and the 1968 Vienna Conventions on Road Traffic, so it recognizes an International Driving Permit issued under either.

driving.text: Slovakia is a party to both the 1949 Geneva and the 1968 Vienna Conventions on Road Traffic, so it recognizes an International Driving Permit issued under either. Whether a permit is required in addition to a national license, and for how long a foreign license may be used, are set by national road law and have not been checked for Slovakia yet.

tips.text: Driving on Slovak motorways requires an electronic vignette (eznamka.sk). Buy it online before crossing the border; enforcement is by camera and fines are steep.
Mountain rescue in the Tatras can be charged to uninsured hikers. Carry insurance that covers mountain rescue, check avalanche and storm warnings, and note the rescue number 18 300.
Bratislava is under an hour from Vienna by train or bus with no border checks inside Schengen — the two capitals pair easily in one trip.
Visa-waiver nationals will need an ETIAS travel authorization once the EU system becomes mandatory. Check the official EU website for the current status before traveling.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Slovakia?
faq.answer: EU/EEA and Swiss citizens enter freely with a passport or ID card. Citizens of some 60 visa-waiver countries — including the US, UK, Canada, Australia, Japan and most of the Americas — get 90 days in any 180-day period across the Schengen Area. Everyone else needs a Schengen visa from a Slovak embassy or visa center.

faq.question: Is Slovakia in the Schengen Area?
faq.answer: Yes, since 2007. There are no border checks when arriving from other Schengen countries, and your 90/180-day visa-free allowance is counted across the entire area, not per country.

faq.question: Will I need ETIAS for Slovakia?
faq.answer: Once the EU's ETIAS system becomes mandatory, visa-waiver travelers will need to obtain the online authorization before their trip. It is expected to cost a small fee, be valid for three years, and cover the whole Schengen Area. Check the official EU site for the launch date.

faq.question: What currency does Slovakia use?
faq.answer: The euro, since 2009 — unlike neighboring Czechia, Poland and Hungary, which keep their own currencies. Cards are accepted almost everywhere.

faq.question: Can I hike the High Tatras year-round?
faq.answer: No. Many high-mountain trails close seasonally from November 1 to June 15 for safety and conservation, and snow lingers into early summer. Valley walks and ski resorts operate through winter; check trail status locally before setting out.
